## The Core Cognitive Engine: The Systems Loop

Unlike purely linear thinkers or purely emotional feelers, Chris perceives the world as an interconnected web of dependencies:

```
  [ Components ]
        ↓
  [ Relationships ]
        ↓
  [ Dependencies ]
        ↓
  [ Rules & Mechanisms ]
        ↓
  [ Emergent System ]
        ↓
  [ Observable Behavior ]
```

::: {.comic-panel}
::: {.comic-caption}
THE CHRIS ALGORITHM
:::
> **Understand the system → Decompose it → Identify the rules → Modify it → Test it → Improve it → Make it understandable to others.**

Chris is never satisfied with merely getting an outcome by accident. He needs to know **why the outcome happened** and **whether the underlying mechanism is true, fair, and coherent**.
:::

## Undocumented Quirks (Features, Not Bugs!)

Every advanced operating system comes with unique quirks. Knowing them in advance will save you hours of confusion:

::: {.callout-note}
## 🤓 Quirk #1: The Hyperfixation Deep Dive
When Chris encounters a compelling system, game, technology, or topic, expect intense focus and rapid knowledge acquisition. 

* **Symptoms:** 30 browser tabs open, spontaneous mini-lectures, eyes glowing with excitement.
* **Pro-Tip:** Ask questions! Seeing someone engage with his current passion is one of the quickest ways to Chris's heart.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## ⚠️ Quirk #2: Sensitivity to Being Misunderstood or Forgotten
Because Chris invests deeply in relationships and systems, feeling dismissed, misunderstood, or forgotten hits his emotional firmware hard.

* **Trigger:** Casual brushing off of an idea he deeply cares about, or unanswered messages during moments of vulnerability.
* **Remedy:** Reassure with presence: *"I hear you, I care about what you're saying, let's talk about it."*
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## 💡 Quirk #3: The "Turbulent (-T)" Introspection Loop
The Turbulent trait means Chris is highly conscientious and self-reflective. He deeply cares about doing the right thing and being a good partner, which sometimes leads to overthinking:

* **Internal monologue:** *"Did I phrase that clumsily? Are they secretly frustrated with me?"*
* **Remedy:** Explicit words of affirmation! A simple *"I love you and we're totally good"* dissolves 99% of internal background loops.
:::
